overview: The MC85 Star Cruiser is a mon calamari cruiser whose design philosophy reflects the industrial and strategic priorities of Resistance (34 ABY–35 ABY). Resistance-era MC85 cruisers like the Raddus carried heavier shields and ion drives for deep-space retreats. Production estimates place the class at ~25 units, though wartime losses, capture, and black-market duplication make precise fleet registries unreliable.
history:
Engineering teams first finalized the MC85 Star Cruiser blueprints during the political climate of Resistance (34 ABY–35 ABY). The mon calamari cruiser was intended to solve specific fleet gaps—whether planetary assault, convoy escort, starfighter superiority, or terror bombardment—and shipwrights iterated hull plates, reactor output, and crew compartments accordingly.

Once deployed, the MC85 Star Cruiser appeared in fleet actions that defined its reputation. Resistance-era MC85 cruisers like the Raddus carried heavier shields and ion drives for deep-space retreats. Combat logs show crews exploiting the class's strengths while improvising fixes for known weaknesses under fire, a pattern repeated across every major galactic conflict.

As doctrine evolved, rival factions studied captured MC85 Star Cruiser hulls. Refit yards duplicated weapons mounts and sensor suites; some variants never appeared in official manifests. Estimated production of ~25 units therefore understates how many similar silhouettes operated under alternate insignia.

Surviving MC85 Star Cruiser vessels now sit in museum orbits, mercenary fleets, and scrap worlds. Historians treat the class as a measure of how galactic wars industrialize violence—each hull a factory product that outlived the politicians who ordered it.
significance:
The MC85 Star Cruiser demonstrates how mon calamari cruiser design shapes campaign outcomes. Its layout influenced successor programs and remains a case study in naval academies.

With roughly ~25 units hulls associated with Resistance (34 ABY–35 ABY), the class became a visual symbol of its faction's reach—recognizable in holonet footage and feared in convoy manifests.

Engineers still debate whether the MC85 Star Cruiser prioritized firepower over crew survival; that trade-off defines its legacy in both propaganda and honest after-action reports.
